title: Model Common Resource Shapes

# Model Common Resource Shapes

Use these as starting points when deciding how to describe your own
experimental objects. A resource can represent anything trackable: a physical
object, a digital file, an instrument, or a person.

For the mechanics of building templates, see
[Create a Resource Template](resource-template.qmd).

## A data file

Files are usually described by two independent concerns: where the bytes are
and how they were produced. Separate property groups keep those apart, so a
checksum check does not have to know about beamline settings.

```python
with namespace.build_resource_template(
    name="NeXus File",
    type_names=["file", "hdf5", "nexus"],
) as template:
    template.add_properties({
        "file_metadata": [
            {"name": "path", "type": "str", "default": ""},
            {"name": "sha256", "type": "str", "default": ""},
        ],
        "scan": [
            {"name": "beamline", "type": "str", "default": ""},
            {"name": "exposure_time", "type": "float", "default": 0.1, "unit": "s"},
        ],
    })
```

## An instrument

Instruments are long-lived and mostly static. Give them the specifications a
workflow might need to check, and declare units so the numbers are unambiguous.

```python
with namespace.build_resource_template(
    name="UR5 Robot",
    type_names=["instrument", "robot", "ur5"],
) as template:
    template.add_properties({
        "specs": [
            {"name": "reach_mm", "type": "float", "default": 850.0, "unit": "mm"},
            {"name": "payload_kg", "type": "float", "default": 5.0, "unit": "kg"},
        ]
    })
```

## Choosing type names

The `type_names` list is what process template slots match against, so it
deserves some thought.

Order them from general to specific, as in `["instrument", "robot", "ur5"]`. A
slot that requires `instrument` then accepts this robot alongside every other
instrument, while a slot that requires `ur5` accepts only this model. That lets
one workflow be written against `instrument` and another against a specific
model, without either having to name the template.

Keep type names stable. Renaming one breaks every slot that requires it, in the
same way renaming a class breaks its callers.

## Containers and their contents

When one resource physically contains others, such as a plate holding wells,
declare that as a parent-child template relationship rather than as a property.
Child resources get their own identity and can be assigned to process runs
independently. See
[Nest Resource Templates](nested-resource-templates.qmd).
